speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower in view of the recent construction mishap at the TPE-PIE viaduct (a) whether the Ministry will review the current blacklisting framework; (b) how can the Ministry work with BCA to debar blacklisted companies from working on projects rather than just bar them from hiring new workers or renew existing ones; and (c) whether companies need to prove that they have taken remedial steps, including improving worker safety training, before having the blacklist status removed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These two frameworks are reviewed regularly to maintain their effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We issue demerit points to companies that are fined, issued with a Stop Work Order or prosecuted in Courts for safety offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Demerit Point System was amended in 2015 following consultation with the industry and tripartite partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There were two significant changes under this 2015 amendment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: First, the demerit points will last for 18 months, up from 12 months previously.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In the past, they could continue to hire foreign workers but at a higher levy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Companies with poor safety management will be put under the BUS programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Once under the BUS programme, companies will have their bizSAFE certification revoked and be closely supervised by MOM to rectify all identified safety lapses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: BUS was enhanced in 2016 to have broader entry criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Previously, a company needed to have systemic safety infringements to be put under BUS, even if they had a fatal accident.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Since May 2016, any company with a Stop Work Order or any fatality is placed under the BUS programme immediately.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To exit from BUS, companies need to demonstrate to MOM that they have taken sufficient remedial steps to improve their Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This includes conducting refresher training for all workers on any unsafe practices found.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: On average, this process takes at least one year for companies to get out of the BUS programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Since the enhancement, we have placed 25 companies on the BUS programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We are coordinating with other Government agencies, including BCA, to review procurement practices for construction projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Agencies handling key public projects, such as JTC and LTA, already take into consideration bidders' safety record, such as demerit points, bizSAFE or BUS status, in their procurement assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We also make available the list of companies under the BUS programme and the demerit points on our website for reference by those who are interested.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: While we take companies with poor safety records to task, they should also be given an opportunity to improve their safety record and performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In fact, many companies which went through the BUS programme have exited and attained good safety standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Some have even won safety and health awards locally and internationally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM will continue to monitor developments and the situation, and refine our regulatory framework where needed to strengthen WSH performance in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Are we satisfied that there is no systemic failure of its safety management system?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: First, about why OKP was allowed to participate in Government projects despite it being involved in some accident.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: And following the September 2015 accident, MOM inspected all of OKP's worksites to check if the accident reflected a wider systemic failure of the company's safety management.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: However, no evidence of systemic safety lapses was found from the inspections.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, OKP was not placed under BUS following that accident.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, for any company with a workplace fatality now, Government agencies would have known that they are put on BUS and will have their bizSAFE status revoked.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, agencies can take this into account when assessing their upcoming tenders.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This timeline explains why OKP was not put under the BUS programme for the earlier 2015 accident but was placed on the BUS programme following the PIE viaduct accident on 14 July this year.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: But having said that, we are cognisant that, at the construction worksites, things can happen quite quickly and we are not taking this current situation lightly.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: In fact, we have stepped up our enforcement actions on many worksites to make sure that all these worksites follow the WSH regimes and measures carefully.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As a matter of fact, MOM conducts 16,000 inspections a year on all the worksites in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The bulk of our inspections is concentrated on the higher-risk industries, like marine, oil and gas, as well as construction.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, while we cannot say for sure that the current regime will be able to 100% get the companies to adhere fully to the WSH regulations, standards and performance, we will closely monitor them.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: If there is a need to further tighten, we will continue to do so, as the reviewing of our safety regulatory framework is an ongoing effort.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Minister of State said that OKP had some industrial accident but was not put under BUS because it was determined not to be systemic.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask what MOM considers to be a systemic problem for companies which had industrial accidents.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: How does it assess whether it is systemic or not?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And would he tell this House examples of companies which have been found to have systemic problems and put under BUS?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: When we investigate and inspect a company, we look at many aspects, from the company's WSH systems to the daily inspections and also the toolbox meetings conducted by the supervisors and the foremen, and also to investigate the WSH risk assessment procedures for every job.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, it is a very comprehensive regime and inspection to make sure that the companies, from the management to the workers, follow this set of WSH standards and guidelines.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: If a company has encountered a certain worksite accident and the cause of the accident is not because there were no proper WSH regimes or regulations put in place but because of certain human errors or oversight, that is considered as an isolated case and not a systemic failure.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We will use this as a basis to evaluate the company's standards of the WSH and then decide whether this company has a systemic widespread WSH failure or the accident was caused by an isolated, incidental or, sometimes, human error.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I do not have the list of the companies at this moment.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, I will give it to the Member offline.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To what extent are there safeguards in place against the directors of a company that may be under some form of blacklisting, be it under BUS or some other regime, from incorporating a new company and bidding for Government projects and, thereby, potentially evading their previous negative safety records?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If there are no safeguards against them now, will the Ministry look into that and introduce some safeguards against them?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The records follow the individuals rather than the company.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, if a company director has infringed certain WSH regulations and all that, there is a record against him.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: That record will go with him, even if he sets up a new company.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, there is little chance that individuals can evade our system by setting up different companies to undertake Government or private sector projects.
